title: Generators that are either off or above their minimum

blocks.text: A small island grid schedules its diesel units for the next hour. Each unit in `units` has a name, a minimum output `min_mw` and a maximum `max_mw`. A unit is either off, and then it makes no power at all, or on, and then it must run at least at its minimum: a diesel engine cannot idle at 3 MW when its minimum stable load is 10 MW.

The model in `units.py` already has, for every unit $`u`$, a binary $`\text{on}_u`$ and a continuous output $`0 \le p_u \le \text{max}_u`$, and a row making the units meet the hour's demand. Write `add_unit_rules(model, on, power, units)` so that the model states the two rules, each as one MathOpt indicator constraint per unit:

With $`p_u \ge 0`$ as a bound, $`p_u \le 0`$ means $`p_u = 0`$, and the bound $`p_u \le \text{max}_u`$ already caps a running unit. Each implied row has one side, which is what SCIP accepts (lesson 4.3.1).
`on` and `power` are dicts keyed by unit name. Name the constraints `off_<name>` and `on_<name>`.

The tests fix each unit's on/off state and output, and ask SCIP whether the model accepts that hour, so any correct way of writing the two rules passes. HiGHS would refuse the model: lesson 4.3.1 shows which solvers take indicator constraints. About six lines.

cases.says: a unit that is off and makes no power is allowed, and one that is off but makes power is refused
a unit that is on at or above its minimum is allowed, and one that is on below it is refused
a second unit with a higher minimum is refused at a level the first unit's minimum would allow

origin.section: An Indicator Constraint Is a Binary, a Row and the Value That Switches It On

concepts: an implication written as an indicator constraint, switched on at zero or at one, with one or two bounds
